claim: Asymmetric Notch (N) signaling inhibits intestinal stem cell (ISC) self-renewal by promoting ISC differentiation into enteroblast (EB) in adult Drosophila midgut.
source: In adult Drosophila midgut, asymmetric Notch (N) signaling inhibits intestinal stem cell (ISC) self-renewal by promoting ISC differentiation into enteroblast (EB).
evidence: This is a well-established finding in the field, supported by citations in the manuscript.

claim: Epithelium-derived Bone Morphogenetic Protein (BMP) promotes ISC self-renewal by antagonizing N pathway activity.
source: We have previously shown that epithelium-derived Bone Morphogenetic Protein (BMP) promotes ISC self-renewal by antagonizing N pathway activity (Tian and Jiang, 2014).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to previous work by the authors.

claim: Loss of BMP signaling results in ectopic N pathway activity even when the N ligand Delta (Dl) is depleted.
source: Here, we show that loss of BMP signaling results in ectopic N pathway activity even when the N ligand Delta (Dl) is depleted
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data presented in Figure 1 showing N pathway activation in Put and Dl double RNAi guts.

claim: The N inhibitor Numb acts in parallel with BMP signaling to ensure a robust ISC self-renewal program.
source: the N inhibitor Numb acts in parallel with BMP signaling to ensure a robust ISC self-renewal program.
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data showing that Numb becomes crucial when BMP signaling is compromised.

claim: Numb is asymmetrically segregated in about 80% of dividing ISCs.
source: Although Numb is asymmetrically segregated in about 80% of dividing ISCs, its activity is largely dispensable for ISC fate determination under normal homeostasis.
evidence: This is based on previous studies cited in the manuscript.

claim: Numb activity is largely dispensable for ISC fate determination under normal homeostasis.
source: Although Numb is asymmetrically segregated in about 80% of dividing ISCs, its activity is largely dispensable for ISC fate determination under normal homeostasis.
evidence: This is supported by data showing that numb mutant clones can retain ISCs under homeostatic conditions.

claim: Numb becomes crucial for ISC self-renewal when BMP signaling is compromised.
source: However, Numb becomes crucial for ISC self-renewal when BMP signaling is compromised.
evidence: This is supported by experimental data showing ISC loss in mad numb double mutants.

claim: Neither Mad RNA interference nor its hypomorphic mutation led to ISC loss.
source: Whereas neither Mad RNA interference nor its hypomorphic mutation led to ISC loss
evidence: This is supported by experimental data in Figures 2 and 3.

claim: Inactivation of Numb in Mad RNAi or mad hypomorphic mutation backgrounds resulted in stem cell loss due to precocious ISC-to-EB differentiation.
source: inactivation of Numb in these backgrounds resulted in stem cell loss due to precocious ISC-to-EB differentiation.
evidence: This is supported by experimental data in Figures 2, 3, and 4.

claim: Numb mutations resulted in stem cell loss during midgut regeneration in response to epithelial damage that causes fluctuation in BMP pathway activity.
source: Furthermore, we find that numb mutations resulted in stem cell loss during midgut regeneration in response to epithelial damage that causes fluctuation in BMP pathway activity
evidence: This is supported by experimental data in Figure 6 showing increased ISC loss in numb mutants after bleomycin treatment.

claim: The asymmetrical segregation of Numb into the future ISC may provide a fail-save mechanism for ISC self-renewal by offsetting BMP pathway fluctuation.
source: suggesting that the asymmetrical segregation of Numb into the future ISC may provide a fail-save mechanism for ISC self-renewal by offsetting BMP pathway fluctuation, which is important for ISC maintenance in regenerative guts.
evidence: This is a speculative interpretation of the experimental findings.

claim: Drosophila midgut is an equivalent of mammalian small intestine.
source: Drosophila midgut, an equivalent of mammalian small intestine, has emerged as a powerful system to study stem cell biology in adult tissue homeostasis and regeneration (Casali and Batlle, 2009; Jiang and Edgar, 2011; Jiang et al., 2016).
evidence: This is established knowledge in the field, supported by citations.

claim: Intestinal stem cells (ISCs) in adult midguts are localized at the basal side of the gut epithelium.
source: Intestinal stem cells (ISCs) in adult midguts are localized at the basal side of the gut epithelium where they can undergo asymmetric cell division to produce renewed ISCs and enteroblasts (EBs) that differentiate into enterocytes (ECs) (Micchelli and Perrimon, 2006; Ohlstein and Spradling, 2006).
evidence: This is established knowledge supported by citations.

claim: ISCs can undergo asymmetric cell division to produce renewed ISCs and enteroblasts (EBs) that differentiate into enterocytes (ECs).
source: Intestinal stem cells (ISCs) in adult midguts are localized at the basal side of the gut epithelium where they can undergo asymmetric cell division to produce renewed ISCs and enteroblasts (EBs) that differentiate into enterocytes (ECs) (Micchelli and Perrimon, 2006; Ohlstein and Spradling, 2006).
evidence: This is established knowledge supported by citations.

claim: At low frequency, an ISC daughter is fated to preEE/EEP that differentiates into two enteroendocrine (EE) cells after another round of cell division.
source: At low frequency, an ISC daughter is fated to preEE/EEP that differentiates into two enteroendocrine (EE) cells after another round of cell division (Biteau and Jasper, 2014; Beehler-Evans and Micchelli, 2015; Zeng and Hou, 2015; Chen et al., 2018).
evidence: This is established knowledge supported by citations.

claim: About 20% ISCs undergo symmetric cell division to produce two ISCs or two EBs.
source: About 20% ISCs undergo symmetric cell division to produce two ISCs or two EBs (O'Brien et al., 2011; Goulas et al., 2012; Tian and Jiang, 2014).
evidence: This is established knowledge supported by citations.

claim: The decision between ISC self-renewal and differentiation into EB lineage is controlled by Notch (N) signaling whereby N activation drives ISC differentiation into EB.
source: The decision between ISC self-renewal and differentiation into EB lineage is controlled by Notch (N) signaling whereby N activation drives ISC differentiation into EB (Micchelli and Perrimon, 2006; Ohlstein and Spradling, 2006; Ohlstein and Spradling, 2007; Bardin et al., 2010).
evidence: This is established knowledge supported by citations.

claim: The asymmetric N signaling between ISC and EB is influenced by Par/integrins-directed asymmetric cell division and differential BMP signaling.
source: The asymmetric N signaling between ISC and EB is influenced by Par/integrins-directed asymmetric cell division and differential BMP signaling (Goulas et al., 2012; Tian and Jiang, 2014).
evidence: This is established knowledge supported by citations.

claim: EC-produced BMP ligands containing Decapentaplegic (Dpp) and Glass bottom boat (Gbb) heterodimers are secreted basally and concentrated on the basement membrane aligning the basal side of the gut epithelium.
source: EC-produced BMP ligands containing Decapentaplegic (Dpp) and Glass bottom boat (Gbb) heterodimers are secreted basally and concentrated on the basement membrane aligning the basal side of the gut epithelium (Tian and Jiang, 2014).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to previous work.

claim: After asymmetric cell division of ISCs, basally localized daughter cells transduce higher levels of BMP signaling activity than the apically localized daughter cells.
source: After asymmetric cell division of ISCs, basally localized daughter cells transduce higher levels of BMP signaling activity than the apically localized daughter cells and the differential BMP signaling promotes ISC self-renewal by antagonizing N pathway activity through an unknown mechanism (Tian and Jiang, 2014; Tian and Jiang, 2017).
evidence: This is supported by citations to previous work.

claim: The differential BMP signaling promotes ISC self-renewal by antagonizing N pathway activity through an unknown mechanism.
source: After asymmetric cell division of ISCs, basally localized daughter cells transduce higher levels of BMP signaling activity than the apically localized daughter cells and the differential BMP signaling promotes ISC self-renewal by antagonizing N pathway activity through an unknown mechanism (Tian and Jiang, 2014; Tian and Jiang, 2017).
evidence: This is supported by citations to previous work and acknowledges the mechanism is unknown.

claim: The N pathway inhibitor Numb plays a decisive role in asymmetric cell fate determination in Drosophila peripheral and central nervous systems.
source: The N pathway inhibitor Numb plays a decisive role in asymmetric cell fate determination in Drosophila peripheral and central nervous systems whereby Numb segregates asymmetrically into one daughter during division of a neuronal precursor cell and confers distinct fates to the two daughter cells (Uemura et al., 1989; Rhyu et al., 1994; Spana et al., 1995).
evidence: This is established knowledge supported by citations.

claim: Numb segregates asymmetrically into one daughter during division of a neuronal precursor cell and confers distinct fates to the two daughter cells.
source: The N pathway inhibitor Numb plays a decisive role in asymmetric cell fate determination in Drosophila peripheral and central nervous systems whereby Numb segregates asymmetrically into one daughter during division of a neuronal precursor cell and confers distinct fates to the two daughter cells (Uemura et al., 1989; Rhyu et al., 1994; Spana et al., 1995).
evidence: This is established knowledge supported by citations.

claim: The mammalian homologs of Numb are critical for asymmetric fate determination during neurogenesis and myogenesis.
source: The mammalian homologs of Numb are also critical for asymmetric fate determination during neurogenesis and myogenesis (Zhong et al., 1996; Conboy and Rando, 2002; Petersen et al., 2002; Shen et al., 2002; Petersen et al., 2004).
evidence: This is established knowledge supported by citations.

claim: During asymmetric division of an ISC in Drosophila adult midgut, Numb was preferentially segregated into the basally localized daughter that becomes future ISC.
source: Previous studies showed that, during asymmetric division of an ISC in Drosophila adult midgut, Numb was preferentially segregated into the basally localized daughter that becomes future ISC (Goulas et al., 2012; Sallé et al., 2017)
evidence: This is established knowledge supported by citations.

claim: Many numb mutant clones retained ISC after many rounds of cell division although they failed to produce EE.
source: however, many numb mutant clones retained ISC after many rounds of cell division although they failed to produce EE (Bardin et al., 2010; Sallé et al., 2017).
evidence: This is established knowledge supported by citations.

claim: In control guts, most pairs of esg>GFP + precursor cells contained only one Su(H)-lacZ positive cell, indicating that these ISCs divided asymmetrically to produce one ISC and one EB.
source: In control guts, most pairs of esg>GFP + precursor cells, which may represent two recently divided ISC daughters, contained only one Su(H)-lacZ positive cell, indicating that these ISCs divided asymmetrically to produce one ISC and one EB (Figure 1A, B–B'', F).
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 1.

claim: Most esg>GFP + precursor pairs from the Put RNAi guts expressed Su(H)-lacZ in both ISC daughters, suggesting that ISCs underwent symmetric cell division to produce two EBs when Put was depleted.
source: In line with our previous findings, most esg>GFP + precursor pairs from the Put RNAi guts expressed Su(H)-lacZ in both ISC daughters, suggesting that ISCs underwent symmetric cell division to produce two EBs when Put was depleted (Figure 1C–C'', F).
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 1.

claim: esg>GFP+ cells in Dl RNAi guts formed ISC-like tumor clusters that were negative for Su(H)-lacZ.
source: By contrast, esg>GFP+ cells in Dl RNAi guts formed ISC-like tumor clusters that were negative for Su(H)-lacZ (Figure 1D–D'', F)

source: In these guts, esg-GFP+ cells exhibited Su(H)-lacZ expression (Figure 1E–E'', F), suggesting that they activate the N pathway and differentiate into EBs.

source: suggesting that inactivation of both Mad and Numb results in stem cell loss, likely due to precocious ISC-to-EB differentiation.
